name: Au
listed_description: A C++14-compatible physical units library with no dependencies and a single-file delivery option. Emphasis on safety, accessibility, performance, and developer experience.
reason: No numbers against a named baseline reachable. README says 'no runtime performance penalty' with no figures. docs/alternatives/index.md has a 'Compilation Speed' row comparing nholthaus 2.x/3.x, Boost.Units, bernedom/SI, mp-units and Au, but only as qualitative ratings (Au 'Good: not subjectively noticeable'; nholthaus 2.x 'very slow (adds multiple seconds)') plus ratios between competitors (nholthaus 3.x default about 4x the 2.x penalty, mp-units default 2 to 3 times nholthaus, bernedom/SI roughly 2/3 the penalty of Au and Boost) and the page states Au is slower than bernedom/SI; no Au timings. Repo benchmarks/ holds compile-time benchmark sources (BUILD.bazel, defs.bzl) but no published results; issue #759 and PR #799 contain no numbers in the fetched text. The lead's guessed baseline (manual unit conversion) has no benchmark anywhere. Category guess big-integer-arbitrary-precision is wrong: it is a physical-units library.

name: autodiff
listed_description: A modern, fast and expressive C++ library for automatic differentiation.
reason: Own README only says 'efficient'; no benchmark numbers. Its archived .arquive/benchmarks/README.md says 'Currently broken' and only plans a comparison against other implementations. The only numbers found are third-party and show it slower, not faster: buech/ad-benchmarks (Xcelerit, maker of XAD; GCC 13.3, Xeon Platinum 8488C, -O3 -mavx2 -mfma) gives SABR calibration gradient 38 ms for autodiff (forward dual mode) vs CppAD 32 ms, Adept 19 ms, XAD 8.4 ms; autodiff did not finish the Heston MC, XVA CVA and LIBOR swaption benchmarks. If the orchestrator wants a flagged not-faster record, those are the numbers.

name: Chipmunk
listed_description: A fast and lightweight 2D game physics library.
reason: README only says 'fast' and 'Extremely fast impulse solving by utilizing Erin Catto's contact persistence algorithm' with no numbers and no named baseline; repo has no benchmark directory (top level: android, codeblocks, demo, doc-src, doc, include/chipmunk, msvc, objectivec, scripts, src, xcode) and has moved to Codeberg with a GitHub mirror. WebSearch found only forum anecdotes (a Construct 2 forum ranking of Physics, Box2D+ and Chipmunk plugins without figures) and a snippet saying ARM NEON code speeds simulations 20 to 40 percent, which is against Chipmunk's own non-NEON path. The 2D physics benchmark repos found (mtsamis/box2d-benchmarks, joelgwebber/bench2d, Godot Rapier vs Box2D) do not include Chipmunk; the axmol wiki '2D Physics Engines Information' has no numbers; chipmunk-physics.net is blocked. The guessed category blas-lapack is wrong: it is a 2D rigid-body physics library.
